newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-PRIX DE L`ARC DE TRIOMPHE FORM GUIDE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-PRIX DE L`ARC DE TRIOMPHE FORM GUIDE.

text.p: Following is a brief form guide to
the leading fancies in Sunday's Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe
HELISSIO (5-2) - Trained in France by Elie Lellouche, ridden
by Olivier Peslier. Impressive winner over course and distance
in last month's Prix Niel, a reliable Arc guide. Beat Darazari
one of Sunday's chief rivals. French Derby flop but returned to
form to win Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud. Also won Prix Lupin
earlier in the season. Worthy favourite.
ZAGREB (5-1) - Trained in Ireland by Dermot Weld, ridden by
Michael Kinane. Gave Weld his first Irish Derby success when
springing a 20-1 surprise in late June. Very impressive that day
but not raced since because of fast ground. Jockey's big race
record round the globe is second to none, but colt's
inexperience is a worry. Softer ground in his favour, however.
SWAIN (11-2) - Trained in France by Andre Fabre, ridden by
Thierry Jarnet. Third in last year's Arc to English-trained
Lammtarra. Beat Pentire in last month's Prix Foy, another major
Arc trial. Second to Helissio in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud.
Earlier, won Coronation Cup at Epsom. Jockey and trainer are
both Arc specialists. Swain holds first rate chance.
DARAZARI (6-1) - Trained by Alain de Royer-Dupre, ridden by
Gerald Mosse. Easy winner of the Prix Maurice de Nieuil at
Maisons-Laffitte in July and not disgraced when second to
Helissio in the Prix Niel. Owned by Aga Khan who won the Arc
with Akiyda in 1982. Cannot be ruled out.
CLASSIC CLICHE (8-1) - Trained in England by Saeed bin
Suroor, ridden by Frankie Dettori. Jockey won the race last year
on Lammtarra and riding the crest of a very big wave. Colt is a
versatile, classy performer. Won the Ascot Gold Cup and
Doncaster St Leger. Drops back in distance but holds reasonable
chance on good second to Pentire in the King George VI and Queen
Elizabeth Diamond Stakes. Missed a gallop last weekend but back
on course now. Anything Dettori rides has to be respected but
over the shorter distance Classic Cliche may just be outpaced.
PENTIRE (8-1) - Trained in England by Geoff Wragg, ridden by
Michael Hills. Beaten by Swain in the Prix Foy but had to make
his own running which clearly did not suit him. Earlier won the
King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot and
is a top-notch performer. May be less effective on softish
going, but will not go down without a fight.
SHAAMIT (12-1) - Trained in England by William Haggas,
ridden by Pat Eddery. Won Epsom Derby on first appearance of the
season but beaten since in the King George VI and Queen
Elizabeth Diamond Stakes (third) and Irish Champion Stakes
(fourth). Jockey has excellent Arc record with four previous
winners, but Shaamit will need to reproduce his Epsom sparkle.
OSCAR SCHINDLER (14-1) - Trained in Ireland by Kevin
Prendergast, ridden by Cash Asmussen. Improving four-year-old;
easy winner of Irish St Leger and also successful at Royal
Ascot. Only fourth in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth
Diamond Stakes behind Pentire but squeezed for room. Melbourne
Cup possible later in the year. Place prospects.
PILSUDSKI (16-1) - Trained in England by Michael Stoute,
ridden by Walter Swinburn. Last month in Germany, gave Swinburn
his first group one win since returning from a near-fatal injury
in Hong Kong. Good performance to win the race, the Grosser
Preis von Baden, but faces much stiffer test here.
TAMURE (16-1) - Trained in England by John Gosden, ridden by
Freddie Head. Second in last year's Epsom Derby to Lammtarra,
but has not run for nearly a year mainly because the ground has
been too firm. Veteran jockey Head is a late booking but knows
Longchamp intimately and has won the Arc three times, the first
back in 1972 on San San. Very tough task to win race of this
calibre after such a long lay-off.
